description: Total cholesterol is the aggregate measurement of all circulating cholesterol molecules carried by lipoproteins in the bloodstream, including LDL, HDL, and VLDL fractions.
what_it_measures: Measures total circulating cholesterol concentration to assess atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk.

clinical_significance.elevated: Associated with plaque accumulation inside coronary and peripheral arterial walls, increasing risk of coronary artery disease, angina, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke.
clinical_significance.low: Very low cholesterol (< 120 mg/dL) can be observed in severe malnutrition, advanced liver disease, hyperthyroidism, or malabsorption syndromes.

description: Low-density lipoproteins transport cholesterol particles synthesized in the liver to peripheral tissues. When present in excess, LDL penetrates endothelial lining of arterial walls, becomes oxidized, and forms atherosclerotic plaques.
what_it_measures: Quantifies circulating atherogenic low-density lipoprotein cholesterol; primary target of lipid-lowering statin therapy.

reference_ranges.optimal: Below 100 mg/dL (Below 70 mg/dL or 55 mg/dL for high/very high ASCVD risk patients)

clinical_significance.elevated_ldl: Directly linked to atheroma formation, coronary stenosis, and cardiovascular events. Managed through lifestyle modifications, statins, ezetimibe, or PCSK9 inhibitors.
clinical_significance.low_ldl: Achieved with aggressive statin/PCSK9 therapy; intrinsically low levels occur in abetalipoproteinemia.

description: High-density lipoproteins participate in reverse cholesterol transport, scavenging excess cholesterol from arterial tissues and foam cells and transporting it back to the liver for catabolism and biliary excretion.
what_it_measures: Measures cardioprotective high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels.

reference_ranges.low_heart_disease_risk_factor: Below 40 mg/dL for men; Below 50 mg/dL for women
reference_ranges.acceptable: 40 - 59 mg/dL for men; 50 - 59 mg/dL for women

clinical_significance.low_hdl: Recognized independent risk factor for coronary heart disease, metabolic syndrome, and insulin resistance. Often exacerbated by sedentary lifestyle, obesity, smoking, and high refined carbohydrate diet.
clinical_significance.high_hdl: Protective against atherosclerosis, though extremely high levels (> 100 mg/dL) due to genetic CETP mutations may not confer additional protection.

description: Triglycerides are the main chemical form of energy storage in adipose tissue, derived from dietary fats and hepatic lipogenesis from excess carbohydrates.
what_it_measures: Measures blood triglyceride concentration in fasting state.

clinical_significance.hypertriglyceridemia: Levels > 150 mg/dL contribute to metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD/MASLD), and cardiovascular disease. Extreme elevations (> 500 - 1,000 mg/dL) present significant danger of acute necrotizing pancreatitis.
clinical_significance.low_triglycerides: Can reflect malnutrition, low-fat diets, or hyperthyroidism.
